Hi Alice — great to meet earlier, appreciate the clear goals. Quick recap + concrete next steps below.

Recap / recommendations (high level):
- Generator (quality/cost tiers):
  • Redwood-3-small: low-cost, good for high-throughput summarization; useful for interactive search where strict grounding is enforced.
  • Redwood-13b-instruct: balanced quality/cost for most Q&A scenarios — recommended for pilot.
  • Redwood-70b (or fine-tuned variant): high-quality option if you need best-in-class answers and can accept higher cost.

- Embeddings: "redwood-embed-1" for production (dense, stable vector space). If you want cheaper options for large-scale batch indexing, we can provide a quantized embed profile.

- Retriever settings:
  • Start with dense retrieval (FAISS/HNSW) using precomputed embeddings; top_k_retriever = 50 as a default for 100–200k docs.
  • Use hybrid scoring (bm25 + dense) if you have many short FAQ-like docs — this often reduces missed recalls.

- Reranker:
  • Cross-encoder (our re-ranker-cross-encoder-1) for highest grounding precision — use as a second-stage reranker on top_k_retriever -> top_m = 5.
  • Lightweight dual-encoder reranker can be used for latency-sensitive paths (distilled reranker or a distilled cross-encoder).

- Grounding / quality metrics to track:
  • Grounding precision (fraction of generated assertions supported by retrieved spans).
  • Hallucination rate (manual label or heuristic-based).
  • Answer latency (retrieval + reranker + generate).
  • Token cost per query.

Attachments & links:
- Eval guide + sample prompt sets (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-rag-prompt-sets
- Pilot benchmark doc: https://redwood-internal.company/benchmarks/acme-rag-2027
- I've attached a short summary of our recommended eval run (eval_results_summary.pdf) for your team to use.

Next steps / action items:

2) Redwood (Rafael + Ben) to provision a benchmark run (redwood-13b-instruct + redwood-embed-1 + re-ranker-cross-encoder-1) and share latency / grounding metrics within 48 hours.

Hi Alice — quick technical follow-up on latency/cost and recommended config for the pilot run.

Benchmark config we'll run (pilot):
- Embedding model: redwood-embed-1 (precompute vectors for corpus).
- Index: FAISS HNSW, IVF_PQ for 120k docs with sharding; top_k_retriever = 50.
- Reranker: re-ranker-cross-encoder-1 as a second-stage (running on a small GPU for the benchmark); top_m = 5.
- Generator: redwood-13b-instruct with generation length cap tuned to your expected answer length.

Latency & cost estimates (approx):
- Embedding lookup (FAISS) + hybrid scoring: ~8–20ms median depending on shard topology.
- Cross-encoder reranker (5 candidates) on small GPU: ~25–60ms median; CPU fallback ~120–250ms.
- Generator (13B) streaming median: ~80–150ms depending on answer length and prompt length.
- End-to-end median estimate: ~120–230ms for the config above (network + serving overhead added ~10–30ms). P95 will depend on load and whether CPU fallback occurs.

Cost ballpark (incremental) per 1k queries:
- Embedding + retrieval + rerank + generate (13B) — rough estimate: $8–$18 per 1k queries (depends heavily on generator token output and batching). We'll provide a refined cost after the benchmark run with your sample prompts.

Caching: session-level caching of user queries will materially reduce generator and reranker load for repeated queries; caching hits cut both cost and latency substantially. Prefix/KV caching is less relevant here unless you keep long context windows.

Grounding metrics & instrumentation suggestions:
- Grounding precision: percent of generated claims with an explicit supporting span in retrieved docs (automated by overlap heuristics + manual sampling).
- Grounding recall: percent of relevant documents retrieved in top_k.
- Hallucination rate: manual label set on 200 queries + heuristics.
- Latency breakdown by stage: retrieval / reranker / generator / network.

Attachments: I've attached a short CSV of our rough reranker latency estimates to help with perf planning (reranker_latency_estimates.csv).

We'll kick off the benchmark when we receive the sample docs + queries. I'll post results in HubSpot (HS-ACME-00042) and share a summary doc.

Cheers,
